# EZ Hanseikai

EZ Hanseikai is a Windows app where a team records its games and reviews them together. A room holds the team's recordings. Each recording has events (notes, marks, analysis results such as match ends and spoken lines), and the room has one game plan: a Markdown page.

This file describes the app's local HTTP API. An AI agent or a program can read recordings and write notes and the game plan. Whatever you write is shared with the whole room, like what people write in the app.

## Turn it on

The API is off by default. A person turns it on in the app: Settings > API > Local API, or starts the app with --api (or EZH_API=1). The address is http://127.0.0.1:47625 and Copy token puts the token on the clipboard. While the API runs, the address and the token are also in api.json in the app's data folder (%LOCALAPPDATA%\\dev.ez-hanseikai.app), readable by the current Windows user only. The token is secret; never print it into notes or the game plan.

## Rules

- Every request except GET /llms.txt needs the header `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.
- The Host header must be 127.0.0.1:47625 or localhost:47625. With Settings > API > Other devices, the PC's own addresses and name with the same port work too. There is no CORS.
- JSON in, JSON out (UTF-8). Errors are `{"error": "..."}` with the status 400, 401, 403, 404, 405, 409 or 413.
- Times in a recording are seconds from its start (`at_s`, `from_s`, `to_s`, rounded to 0.1). Clock times are milliseconds since 1970 (`start_ms`, `end_ms`).
- Reads work for every room on this PC. Writes work only for the room that is open in the app (409 otherwise); ask the person to open it.
- Notes are at most 500 characters and the game plan at most 4000. Write `#tag` in a note text to tag it, or send `tags`.
- Paths are on this PC (write them like C:/videos/scrim). A recording comes in as video files or a session folder and leaves as a folder of plain files; the format is in docs/session-format.md of the repository.

## Read

GET /v1
  {"app": "EZ Hanseikai", "version": "0.12.0", "id": "...", "name": "Ann", "room": "<open room id or null>", "recording": false}

GET /v1/status
  {"room": "<open room id or null>", "recording": false, "state": "standby", "members": [{"id": "...", "name": "Ann", "online": true, "state": "standby"}]}
  state is offline, idle (no screen shared), standby (sharing a screen) or recording. The top-level state is this PC's; members are those of the open room.

GET /v1/rooms
  {"rooms": [{"id": "ab12", "name": "Practice", "active": true, "members": [{"id": "...", "name": "Ann", "online": true}]}]}

GET /v1/rooms/{room}/recordings
  {"recordings": [{"id": "2026-10-19 21-30-00", "kind": "play", "recording": false, "start_ms": 1792445400000, "end_ms": 1792448100000, "length_s": 2700.0, "members": [{"id": "...", "name": "Ann", "voice_only": false, "start_ms": 1792445400000, "end_ms": 1792448100000}]}]}
  Newest first. A recording that was imported also has "title", "imported_by" ({"id", "name"}) and "imported": true on its members (the views). kind is "play" or "debrief" (a recording of people talking while they watched another one). recording is true while it is being recorded. Put the id in the URL with spaces as %20.

GET /v1/rooms/{room}/recordings/{recording}
  One element of the list above.

GET /v1/rooms/{room}/recordings/{recording}/events[?tag=rotate][&kind=note]
  {"events": [{"key": "<author>/<id>", "id": 1792445520000000, "author": "...", "author_name": "Ann", "plugin": null, "kind": "note", "at_s": 120.5, "to_s": null, "member": null, "member_name": null, "text": "Rotate early #rotate", "tags": ["rotate"], "values": null}]}
  Notes, marks and analysis results in time order (untimed ones first). plugin is the plugin's name for analysis results, null for people. kinds: note, mark, match_end, ... Spoken lines, drawings and the game plan are left out unless you ask with kind=speech, kind=drawing or kind=board.

GET /v1/rooms/{room}/recordings/{recording}/chapters
  {"chapters": [{"n": 1, "name": "Match 1", "from_s": 0.0, "to_s": 612.3}, {"n": 2, "name": "Match 2", "from_s": 612.3, "to_s": null}]}
  Matches found by the Apex matches plugin (empty when it is off or found none). to_s is null for the match still in progress.

GET /v1/rooms/{room}/recordings/{recording}/transcript[?member=<id>]
  {"lines": [{"member": "...", "member_name": "Ren", "from_s": 5.0, "to_s": 8.0, "text": "Drop north"}]}
  Spoken lines from the Transcription plugin, in time order (empty when it is off or not finished).

GET /v1/rooms/{room}/board
  {"text": "# This week\n...", "author": "...", "author_name": "Ann", "updated_ms": 1792445000000}
  text is "" when nobody has written the game plan.

GET /v1/rooms/{room}/plugins
  {"plugins": [{"id": "transcribe", "name": "Transcription", "version": "1.0.0", "on": true, "settings": {"model": "small"}, "ready": true, "process_here": true, "workers": [{"id": "...", "name": "Ren", "on": true, "ready": true}]}]}

GET /v1/rooms/{room}/jobs
  {"jobs": [{"job": "...", "plugin": "transcribe", "version": "1.0.0", "set": "<recording id>", "owner": "...", "owner_name": "Ren", "whole": false, "state": "waiting", "by": null, "error": null}], "running": null}
  state is waiting, claimed, done or failed; by is who runs or ran it.

## Write

POST /v1/rooms/{room}/recordings/{recording}/events
  {"text": "Late rotate, ring was closing", "at_s": 1325.5, "tags": ["mistake", "rotate"]}
  Adds a note (kind "note", the default) or a mark ({"kind": "mark", "at_s": 40}; a mark needs at_s and has no text). at_s is optional for a note: without it the note belongs to the whole recording. Tags are added to the text as #tag. Answer 201 with the event, as in the list above.

PUT /v1/rooms/{room}/board
  {"text": "# This week\n**Goal: move before the ring closes**\n\n## Next match\n- Pick the drop first"}
  Replaces the game plan for the whole room. Read it first and keep what still applies. Answer 200 with the board. The format: `#` is the title, a bold line is the goal, each `##` is a card of bullet points; [text](ezh://moment/<recording id>/<seconds>/all) links open a moment.

POST /v1/rooms/{room}/open
  No body. Opens the room in the app, so that writes go to it. Answer 200 {"room": "ab12"}; 409 while this PC records. Starting and stopping a recording is not possible through the API.

POST /v1/rooms/{room}/recordings/import
  {"folder": "C:/videos/Scrim night", "title": "Scrim night", "names": ["Ann", "Ben"]}   or   {"files": ["C:/videos/ann.mp4", "C:/videos/ben.mp4"]}
  Makes a recording from a session folder (session.json is optional; every video file is a view named after the file, offsets 0, the folder name is the title) or from video files, and shares it with the room. title and names (one per view) are optional. Answer 201 {"id": "...", "views": 2, "notes": 0} when done; 400 says what is wrong with the files; 409 when the room is not the open one.

POST /v1/rooms/{room}/recordings/{recording}/export
  {"folder": "C:/exports/scrim", "aligned": false}
  Writes the recording into a new or empty folder: one mp4 per view, session.json, notes.csv, chapters.vtt and subtitles. aligned pads the files so all start together. Answer 201 {"folder": "...", "files": 2, "skipped": []}.

session.json example (every field optional): {"title": "Scrim vs Team B", "start": "2026-10-19T12:30:00Z", "views": [{"name": "Ann", "file": "Ann.mp4"}, {"name": "Ben", "file": "Ben.mp4", "offset_ms": 2500}], "events": [{"at_s": 84.5, "text": "Late rotate #rotate"}, {"at_s": 0, "to_s": 612.3, "text": "Match 1"}]}. Times in a recording are seconds from start.

## Recipes

- Notes from the transcript: GET the transcript and chapters, read them, then POST a note at the time of each decision or mistake with a tag. Check the existing events first so you do not repeat notes.
- Game plan from a recording: GET events, chapters and transcript, then PUT a short board: a goal and a few cards of what to do next.
- A made video (a walkthrough, a highlight reel): put the mp4 in a folder, POST the folder to import, then POST notes at the moments that matter; everyone in the room can watch it in the player.
- Mistakes in a match: GET chapters, take one match's from_s and to_s, read the transcript and events between them, and POST a note with the tag mistake at each moment.

Examples (replace the token and ids):

  curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" http://127.0.0.1:47625/v1/rooms
  curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"text":"Good call #callout","at_s":84}' "http://127.0.0.1:47625/v1/rooms/ab12/recordings/2026-10-19%2021-30-00/events"
